method: Independent read-only review of implementation and existing execution contracts. The reviewer authored separate browser regressions; root runs the final browser and full test suites.
scope: Bounded plain EnsembleSpec and options, captured model and deterministic sample plan
Shared wall deadline, reported node operations and timestamp plus output-element recording accounting
Validated failed/cancelled partial results, hard budget termination and cancellation races
Late executor/Worker responses, current execution sequence, reset and bounded history writes
Exact scalar real output, unit and observation-grid admission; completed-only sample statistics
Actual Worker semantic hash, engine version and replay-model provenance
Explicit completed sample application and current-model semantic-key guard
Local input/output security boundaries and inert React-rendered text

findings.title: Live dashboard edits could alter a planned Worker model without preserving its execution provenance
findings.before: runEnsemble returned only executeInWorker(...).result. Discrete dashboard controls remained active during an ensemble and queueDashboardEvent could send live events to that Worker. The Worker produced a replayModel and a changed semanticHash, but the ensemble wrapper discarded these and admitted the result against the precompiled planned model/hash.
reproduction: Use a discrete dashboard.control model feeding a supported uncertain math.gain and scalar sink.
Start an ensemble, pause the first actual Worker at a progress boundary, switch to the dashboard, change the control value and resume.
The original wrapper could label the changed raw samples with an event-free planned variant, breaking repeatability from its recorded snapshot.
findings.correction: App blocks dashboard event delivery while sweepAbort.current is active. The M23 executor wrapper verifies expected variant SHA-256, ENGINE_VERSION and absence of replayModel for both WorkerRun and WorkerRunError; mismatches become ENSEMBLE_WORKER_PROVENANCE and stop further samples. Source review verified the guard is in runEnsemble; the M19 wrapper was restored after an initial edit matched its similar block.
regressions: M23 live dashboard edits are rejected during an ensemble and actual Worker samples keep the captured model provenance
M23 a mismatched semantic hash on an actual Worker result stops the plan without admitting fabricated provenance

verification.status: both regressions passed on the final display build

reviewedContracts: Inputs use descriptor-based plain-object/dense-array validation before access, numerical bounds and explicit target allowlists. Model, spec and all candidate draws are captured before execution.
Each candidate receives a frozen cloned model and remaining budget. Validated result snapshots charge every timestamp and all recorded legacy output elements plus actual reported runtime operations.

Failed partial results are retained and excluded from statistics. Ordinary validated numerical failures may continue; budget/limit/timeout diagnostics, unvalidated results and errors without a result stop the plan.

A separate abort race and shared deadline prevent waiting indefinitely for an executor. Responses delivered after cancellation do not mutate records or progress. App reset increments activeRun and clears the ensemble report; pending history writes check their sequence after asynchronous manifest creation.

The selected output must be legacy real float64 scalar with an exactly matching unit. Other recorded typed/structured sinks are rejected before execution. Aggregation demands exact raw time-grid identity and never interpolates.

Statistics admit completed records only, disclose n-minus-one sample SD and linear n-minus-one quantiles, return null SD for one completed record and reject nonfinite derived statistics while preserving raw runs.

Only the latest five completed ordinary executions are candidates for the existing bounded history store. Model coefficients change through a user-visible completed sample apply action with current semantic-key/busy/invalid-draft checks.

No new network service, credentials, authentication, database access or personal-information collection is introduced. React text escaping is preserved; imported models and executor results remain bounded data.
limitations: Operations and recordedValues report only validated returned results. In-flight work interrupted by an abort race or an executor error without a result has unknown usage; no subsequent sample executes after such an outcome.
Cancellation does not perform additional aggregation. Completed raw runs remain in records; statistics are explicitly unavailable.
The retained-model snapshot preflight measures projected serialized base-model bytes; runtime/result recording has a separate bounded element budget.
This is a focused implementation review, not a production deployment or general repository security audit.
Final browser execution and final source SHA-256 synchronization are performed by root.
finalSourceNotes: Root synchronized final hashes after UI axis-range clamping and a whitespace-only App correction.
Constant positive/negative Number.MAX_VALUE graph limits remain finite in the final 44 UI tests; final M23 browser suite passes.
